english.title: Fail to keep controlled drugs in a locked receptacle
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person to whom regulation 5 of the Misuse of Drugs (Safe Custody) Regulations 1973 applied, and who had possession of a controlled drug, namely **(..SPECIFY DRUG..), which was kept otherwise than in a locked safe, cabinet or room which was so constructed and maintained as to prevent unauthorised access to the drug, failed to ensure that, so far as circumstances permitted, it was kept in a locked receptacle which could be opened only by you or by a person authorised by you
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 5(1) of the Misuse of Drugs (Safe Custody) Regulations 1973 and section 18(1) of, and Schedule 4 to, the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: As per regulation 5(2), this offence does not apply to a person to whom the drug has been supplied by or on the prescription of a practitioner for his own treatment or that of another person or an animal; a person engaged in the business of a carrier when acting in the course of that business; or a person engaged in the business of a postal operator when acting in the course of that business.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine. not exceeding the prescribed sum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
